newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Garanti gets $150-mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Garanti gets $150-mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Turkey's private Garanti Bankasi has received a $150-million syndicated loan, assistant general manager Husnu Akhan said on Friday.
The accord for the one-year loan, arranged by Dresdner Bank Luxembourg S.A., NationsBank N.A., NatWest Capital Markets, The Sanwa Bank Limited and Societe Generale, was signed last week.
Akhan did not disclose the terms of the loan, but banking sources said the facility carried interest at 50 basis points over LIBOR and all-in cost of 70 basis points over LIBOR.

Garanti had secured a $110 million loan from a syndicate of banks under a club deal in March and signed an accord last month to issue $150 million of commercial paper in the United States under a programme arranged by Bank of America.
Akhan said the pricing and amount of the loan, arranged on a best effort basis, "proved Garanti's credibility" in international markets.

Bankers say some Turkish bank loan deals, mandated earlier this year, have been shelved because of political uncertainities and concerns over the economic policies of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan who took office in late June. -- Servet Yildirim, Istanbul Newsroom, 90-212-275 0875
